chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Aban, and others, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), saying:

Whoever seals his fasting with a righteous saying and a righteous deed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will accept his fasting. It was said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, what is the righteous saying? He said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah, and the righteous deed is the payment of Fitra (alms).

key_terms.شَهَادَةُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: Testimony that there is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What constitutes the righteous saying and deed that ensure the acceptance of fasting according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the spiritual efficacy of fasting is contingent upon concluding it with the Shahadah and the payment of Fitra, linking ritual worship with social responsibility. This specific definition of 'righteous deed' as Fitra highlights the Shia emphasis on the purification of wealth and the communal obligation of charity as integral to the completion of the fast.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hussain Sa’d-Abadi, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammed bin Ziyad, from Aban, and others, from al-Sadiq, Ja’far bin Muhammed, peace be upon them both, that he said:

The one who seals his fasting with a righteous saying and a righteous deed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will accept his fasting. It was then said to him: O son of Allah’s Messenger, what is the righteous saying? He said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah, and the righteous deed is to extract the (alms tax related to) Fitra.
